clue.text: Bean leaf salad plant cultivated for pest control

indicators.note: a salad is a mixture tossed together, so the letters of bean leaf are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: A salad of beans and leaves sounds like a gardener's crop grown to keep insects off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salad' looks like part of the menu, but it is the anagram signal applied to BEAN LEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like herb takes its name from the old belief that it drove away fleas, hence grown against pests.

clue.text: Instruction to leave on departing street

indicators.note: departing means the letters for 'on' leave the word street

parts.note: on means re, as in 'regarding' or 'about'

explanation.surface: Someone is told to stay put while leaving along a road.
explanation.walkthrough: RE ('on', meaning concerning) departs from STREET.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's Latin mark meaning 'let it stand', telling the printer to leave text unchanged.

clue.text: Model filling musical coffers

indicators.note: filling means one piece goes inside the other, packed into its middle

parts.note: Chess is the stage musical by Tim Rice with Benny and Björn of ABBA
the Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model gives T

explanation.surface: A fashion model is paid out of the profits of a hit musical.
explanation.walkthrough: The Model T Ford gives T, which goes inside CHESS, the musical.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffers are strongboxes for valuables, and large lidded boxes of that kind are synonyms.

clue.text: The Bard rewritten for example right to left on page

definitions.text: for example right to left on page

indicators.note: rewritten means the letters of the words the bard are written out again in another order

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's text is reworked, perhaps printed in a right-to-left script.
explanation.walkthrough: THE BARD is rewritten. The definition gives one example of the measurement: the distance across a page from one side to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Width, the side-to-side measurement, is what you cover crossing a page from right edge to left.

clue.text: Trained climber with regard to one mistake on ascent

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: with regard to means re, as in a memo heading
one is the Roman numeral I
a lapse is a slip or mistake

explanation.surface: A mountaineer slips up on the way up a peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On ascent' reverses RE + I + LAPSE, upwards in this down clue. 'Climber' means a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fruit tree or shrub trained flat along a wall or trellis; the plant climbs where it is guided.

clue.text: Chap sporting topknot on boat — a military craft

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so the topknot sits on the head of the chap, above him in this down clue
in a down clue on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: a topknot can be a ribbon tied on top of the head, a bow
a chap is a man
a ship is a boat

explanation.surface: A man with his hair in a knot stands on a warship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' means skill, not a vessel: the old military art of archery.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill with the longbow was a battlefield discipline, so archery counts as a craft of war.

clue.text: Description of car borrowed from parent, allegedly

indicators.note: borrowed from means the letters are taken from inside the words parent, allegedly

explanation.surface: Someone claims the car was lent to them by Mum or Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'parent, allegedly', and the surface of a borrowed car fits the answer neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired vehicle is described as a hire car, so the word labels the car's status.

clue.text: Flight attendant, loud lascivious type, shouting

parts.note: F is forte, the musical abbreviation for loud

indicators.note: shouting means the word is spoken out, so we want something said the same as a word for a lascivious type

parts.note: a lecher is a lustful man

explanation.surface: A cabin crew member is a loud, leering lech who yells.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' is the feathers on an arrow, not an aeroplane trip; the attendant is the craftsman who fits them.
explanation.definitionFit: An arrow-maker is the craftsman who fixes feather flights onto shafts, hence one attending to flights.

clue.text: High — like walls in the Pennines

definitions.meaning: built of stone; the Pennines, the hill range running down northern England, are crossed by drystone walls

explanation.surface: Someone is high up on a hill among the walls of northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is slang for drug-intoxicated; the other is made of rock, as Pennine field walls are.

clue.text: Stag party stripped at the far end of Bournemouth

indicators.note: at the far end of means take the last letter of Bournemouth
stripped means the word party loses its outer letters, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A stag do ends in a striptease at a seaside town in southern England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stag party' reads as one phrase; 'Stag' alone is the definition. Bournemouth is an English seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old word for a male deer, especially a red deer stag over five years old.

clue.text: Underworld figure getting free time after prison

indicators.note: after means the rearranged piece comes after the prison word

parts.note: a Stalag was a German prisoner-of-war camp

indicators.note: free means the letters of time are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: A gangster gets out after serving time in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' rearranges TIME into MITE. 'Underworld figure' suggests a gangster but means a formation in a cave, underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A mineral column rising from a cave floor is a figure found in the underground world.

clue.text: Roof supports start to bow in high winds

indicators.note: in means the letter goes inside the word for high winds

parts.note: gales are high winds

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of bow

explanation.surface: The roof's supports begin to buckle in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: The triangular wall ends of a pitched house carry the roof ridge, so they support it.

clue.text: Mad incitement to act, moving from place to place

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
a motive is what drives someone to act

explanation.surface: A crazy provocation to do something while travelling about.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word describes the power of movement, travelling from one place to another.

clue.text: Fluid altering shape

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters of altering flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A liquid keeps changing its form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Altering' looks like the anagram signal, but it is the fodder; 'Fluid' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-sided polygon is a basic geometric figure, an example of a shape.

clue.text: Modern communication founded by network

parts.note: the web is the worldwide network
founded as metal is founded, i.e. cast in a mould

explanation.surface: A new form of messaging set up by a broadcasting network.
explanation.definitionFit: An online live broadcast is a recent internet-age means of reaching an audience.

clue.text: Terracotta Army, for example, mostly standing on a track

indicators.note: in a down clue on means sitting above the following pieces
mostly means the word for standing loses its last letter

parts.note: standing means status, one's rank
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: The Chinese clay soldiers stand on a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Terracotta Army is the buried collection of life-size clay soldiers in Xi'an, China.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of sculpted figures counts as sculpture en masse, and the clay soldiers are one.

clue.text: Type of light that woman shone initially on radio set

parts.note: an arc light is a kind of lamp
her refers to that woman

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of shone

explanation.surface: A woman shines a lamp onto a radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Radio set' is not a wireless but a group of characters on radio: the long-running BBC Radio 4 farming soap.
explanation.definitionFit: The family at the centre of the BBC radio soap set in Ambridge is a cast, or set, on radio.

clue.text: Field soldier under spiritual guidance — miserable wretch

indicators.note: in a down clue under means the soldier sits below the guidance

parts.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a playing field
RE is religious education in British schools
a soldier ant is a kind of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier in the field, with a chaplain's guidance, still feels wretched.
explanation.walkthrough: REC is British for a local park or playing field; RE is Religious Education, a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a coward or traitor, a contemptible person, which matches a wretch.

clue.text: Bald Simpsons men staggered, carrying lard

indicators.note: staggered means every other letter of bald simpsons men is taken, at staggered intervals

explanation.surface: Bald men of The Simpsons stagger along, carrying plenty of fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staggered' looks like an anagram signal, but it picks alternate letters, starting with the second.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fatty, describing tissue that stores fat, so something carrying lard.

clue.text: Men in far distance at first home of cockerel

indicators.note: in means the soldiers go inside the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
men here are soldiers, an army

indicators.note: at first means take the first letter of distance

explanation.surface: Men are seen at first far off in the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface splits 'far distance' as one phrase, but 'far' is kept whole and only the D of 'distance' is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster lives among the farm buildings, in the enclosed yard where poultry roam.

clue.text: A trucker's place, erected on American frame of sorts

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above the next piece
erected means set upright, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: a trucker sits in the cab of a lorry
US is short for the United States, i.e. American

explanation.surface: A lorry driver's cab is set up on an American chassis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Erected' turns CAB upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The bead counting device is built on a frame of wires, so it is a frame of a kind.

clue.text: Company measure ready for Russia in English

parts.note: a peck is an old dry measure of volume

explanation.surface: A firm checks whether it is prepared for Russia, in English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for cash. The Russian coin has several spellings; this is the anglicised one, hence 'in English'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a rouble, so a piece of Russian cash, spelt the English way.

clue.text: Old master of The Hay Wain

definitions.text: Old master of The Hay Wain

parts.words: Old master of The Hay Wain
parts.note: an Old Master suggests the painter Constable, but the master of a hay wain, a farm wagon, is the man who drove it

explanation.surface: Asks who painted Constable's famous picture of a farm cart in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hay Wain is John Constable's painting; 'Old master' tempts a painter's name, but a wain is a wagon.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon driver of old was in charge of a hay cart, so he was its master.

clue.text: Final customer of The Bull, for example, that was captured by Da Vinci

definitions.text: that was captured by Da Vinci

parts.note: last means final

parts.words: customer of The Bull, for example
parts.note: a drinker at a pub sups ale; The Bull is the pub in The Archers, the BBC radio soap

explanation.surface: The pub's final drinker is caught on canvas by Leonardo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bull is the village pub in the radio soap set in Ambridge, chiming with the archery theme; 'captured' means painted.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's mural in Milan shows Christ's final meal with the apostles, a scene he painted.

clue.text: Last bits of boring seminar are exceptionally dull

indicators.note: last bits of means take the final letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: The end of a tedious seminar is unusually dreary.
explanation.definitionFit: A colourless sky or mood is described as drab or dreary, the same as dull.

clue.text: Thematic alternative to The Bull

parts.note: in the archery theme, the centre of the target goes by another name than the bullseye

explanation.surface: Points to another pub name, in a puzzle where The Bull is the pub in The Archers.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle's theme is archery; the bull is the centre of a target, and archers call the central ring by its colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Archers name the innermost scoring ring after the precious metal colour it is painted.

clue.text: Who in Strasbourg very nearly follows the case of 8?

indicators.note: follows means the trimmed word comes after the French word

parts.note: qui is French for who; Strasbourg is a French city

indicators.note: nearly means the word very loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A French question about who almost tails a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 across is the arrow-maker, whose arrows are kept in a case slung on the archer's back.
explanation.definitionFit: An archer's case for holding arrows, the very things made by the craftsman at 8.

clue.text: Fine money

explanation.definitionFit: One sense means excellent, as in solid character; the other names the British pound as currency.
